comparison: Perfect agreement on defocalization problem (C15-C20). Both evaluations support these claims. Peer reviewers suggested alternative approaches (astigmatic lenses) but did not dispute the phenomenon itself.
Perfect agreement on MSD limitations (C21-C24). Both evaluations support these claims as established problems. Peer reviewers requested comparison demonstrations, which authors provided.

Perfect agreement on existing analytical methods review (C25-C28). Both evaluations support these claims. Peer reviewers requested more thorough comparisons with existing methods, which authors added in revision.

Perfect agreement on molecular basis of RARA-HT immobility (C39-C44). Both evaluations support these biological interpretations. Peer reviewers requested additional justification of biological insights, which authors provided.
Perfect agreement on bootstrap aggregation experiments (C45). Both evaluations support this analysis addressing reproducibility and experimental variation.
Perfect agreement on spatial analysis capabilities (C46-C50). Both evaluations support these claims demonstrating SA method utility for subcellular localization studies.
Perfect agreement on tracking artifact observation (C51). Both evaluations support this finding, with peer reviewers noting tracking errors are a general SPT limitation.

Disagreement on anomalous diffusion handling (C53-C58). OpenEval finds claims supported, but peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN due to systematic error for subdiffusive motion and concerns about incomplete handling of anomalous diffusion relevant for nuclear proteins.
Perfect agreement on handling states outside support range (C67-C69). Both evaluations support this practical approach, with method robustness demonstrated in simulations.
Perfect agreement on computational and fundamental challenges (C70-C72). Both evaluations support these technical limitations and computational considerations as adequately explained.

Strong agreement on protein dynamics quantification (C34-C38 overlap, C63 in peer only). Both evaluations support these experimental findings. Peer reviewers requested clarification about experimental setup and replicates, which authors provided.

Strong agreement on comparative performance results (C29-C32 overlap, C33 in OpenEval only). Both evaluations support SA superiority. Peer reviewers requested direct comparisons on biological datasets and clarification of new biological insights, which authors provided.

Strong agreement on localization error characterization (C10-C14 overlap, C2-C3 in peer only). Both evaluations support these technical challenges. Peer reviewers requested additional details about localization precision simulations and PSF data, which authors addressed.

Agreement on practical requirements (C64-C65 overlap). Both evaluations support these as practical requirements. Peer reviewers asked how users identify discretization artifacts, which authors addressed in documentation.

Agreement on fundamental limitations (C73-C74 overlap with C52, C66 in peer). Both evaluations support these as honest assessments of method limitations. Peer reviewers explicitly noted these as 'major shortcomings' that authors acknowledged extensively.
Partial overlap on methodological limitations (C52, C66). OpenEval groups these with C64-C65, while peer reviewers group with C73-C74. Both evaluations support these as acknowledged limitations.
Partial overlap on foundational motivation (C2-C3 shared, C1, C4-C5 in OpenEval only, C10-C14 in peer only). Both evaluations support the technical challenges as foundational context.
Minimal overlap on software availability (C33). OpenEval includes this with main results (C29-C32), while peer reviewers evaluated it separately. Both praised code availability and documentation.

Minimal overlap on biological context (C63). OpenEval groups C59-C63 together on RARA biology and controls, while peer reviewers include C63 with experimental findings (C34-C38). Both evaluations support these claims.
OpenEval evaluated historical development of SPT techniques (C6-C9) as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
